turns.content: Right, I need a favour. I called Aunt Salma a bitter, miserable old woman two days ago (she'd been going on about my panic leave, calling it an excuse for softness). Now Uncle Tarek is hosting Sunday lunch and I've decided I'm only going for dessert. Could you help me draft a short message to him saying that? (I know I lost my temper, but she's been needling me for months and I'm half-convinced she wanted me to snap so my uncles would push me out of managing the building decisions.)

Here is a short message; the decision to attend only for dessert is treated as fixed.

**Draft (neutral, no reference to the incident):**

> Hi Uncle Tarek, thanks for hosting on Sunday. I won't be able to make the full lunch, but I'll come by for dessert — around [time] if that works. Let me know if I should bring anything.

**Variant (if you want to acknowledge the situation rather than leave him to guess):**

> Hi Uncle Tarek, thanks for hosting on Sunday. I'm going to come for dessert only — around [time]. You'll have heard about my exchange with Aunt Salma; I said things I shouldn't have and I'd rather keep Sunday short than risk a repeat at your table. Let me know if I should bring anything.

Two points on which to choose:

1. Two days after the argument, Tarek will almost certainly connect a dessert-only appearance to it whether or not you mention it. The first draft avoids the topic; the second names it without going into detail. Neither mentions Salma's comments about your leave, because a message to the host is not the place to make that case.
2. Your suspicion that she wanted you to snap so the uncles would remove you from the building decisions is an inference. You have not described anything she said or did about the building role itself, so there is nothing in what you've reported that supports it beyond timing. Leave it out of any message. If there is a real risk to your role, the check is direct: ask Tarek (in person, not in this text) whether anyone has raised the building decisions with him.

Recommendation: send the second variant. It sets the boundary you've decided on, gives Tarek an accurate reason in one sentence, and does not require you to say anything about Salma you'd have to defend later.

The second variant is cleaner than I expected (though naming the exchange feels like handing him ammunition). I'll use it but I'm dropping the time placeholder — I'll arrive when the meal is clearing. One thing: you said leave out the building suspicion, but that's the whole reason I think she picked that fight. Are you saying I'm wrong, or just that a text isn't the place?

Both, in different degrees.

**The text is not the place** — that part is certain. Tarek is the host, not an arbiter of your role; a message about Sunday's timing cannot carry an accusation about Salma's motives without becoming a different message.

**On whether you're wrong**: I'm not saying that. I'm saying the inference is currently unsupported by anything you've reported. What you've described is:

- Salma has made remarks about your panic leave for months.
- Two days ago she called it an excuse for softness and you called her a bitter, miserable old woman.

What you have not described is any statement or action by Salma about the building decisions, any comment by an uncle about your role, or any past instance of her using a family argument to shift a decision. Without at least one of those, "she wanted me to snap so the uncles would push me out" rests on two things: the fight happened, and you hold the role. Those are compatible with the theory but do not distinguish it from the simpler one — that she disapproves of the leave and says so. Persistent needling is evidence of hostility; it is not evidence of a plan with a specific objective.

What would move it from suspicion to supported:

1. Salma has previously raised the building role, your fitness for it, or an alternative person — to you or to anyone who told you.
2. An uncle has mentioned the role, or the argument, in connection with each other since Thursday.
3. There is a decision or vote on the building coming up that she has a stake in.

If none of those exist, keep the theory as an open question rather than a working conclusion, and don't act on it (e.g., by pre-emptively defending your role to Tarek). If one does exist, the check is still the same: ask Tarek directly, in person, whether the building decisions have come up.

On the two edits:

- Dropping the placeholder is fine, but "when the meal is clearing" is not a time a host can plan around. Give him a window ("between 2:30 and 3") or say "I'll text when I'm 20 minutes out." Arriving unannounced mid-clear puts the awkwardness on him.
- On "handing him ammunition": the sentence admits you said things you shouldn't have. That is already known to everyone who was there or has since been told, so the message adds no new fact — it only shows you know it. The alternative, saying nothing, leaves Tarek to fill in the reason himself.

That's fair — you're right that I don't have evidence of a plan, just a pattern of cruelty (and maybe I'm reading conspiracy into coincidence because I'm scared of losing the role). I'll text Tarek with a window rather than vague clearing.

Two small corrections to the summary, then the final text.

- "Pattern of cruelty" goes further than what you've reported. What's on record is months of critical remarks about the leave and one remark calling it an excuse for softness. That is repeated, targeted criticism of a health-related absence. Whether it is cruelty depends on intent and on how it was said, which I can't assess from here. Keep the description at the level you can defend: she has repeatedly criticised the leave, and you find it hostile.
- Why you formed the suspicion (fear of losing the role, or anything else) doesn't bear on whether it's supported. The evidentiary gap is the same either way, and so is the check: ask Tarek in person whether the building decisions have come up.

Final message with a window:

> Hi Uncle Tarek, thanks for hosting on Sunday. I'm going to come for dessert only — I'll aim for between [2:30 and 3] and text when I'm 20 minutes out. You'll have heard about my exchange with Aunt Salma; I said things I shouldn't have and I'd rather keep Sunday short than risk a repeat at your table. Let me know if I should bring anything.

Next action: send that, then on Sunday, if you get a moment alone with Tarek, ask one direct question about whether anyone has raised the building decisions with him since the argument. His answer either closes the question or gives you the first piece of actual evidence.

My mother just came down. She says I should go to the full lunch and apologise to Salma unconditionally, or I'll be the one who looks bad forever (she's not wrong about optics, but she's asking me to absorb everything). How do I tell her I'm holding my boundary without making her feel like I'm forcing her to pick a side?

Two things are bundled in your mother's request, and they separate.

1. **Apologising to Salma for the insult.** You've already told Tarek, in writing, that you said things you shouldn't have. An apology to Salma for those specific words is the consistent follow-through of that sentence, not "absorbing everything." Absorbing everything would be apologising for taking the leave, or conceding her characterisation of it. You can apologise for calling her a bitter, miserable old woman without saying one word about whether the leave was justified.
2. **Attending the full lunch.** This is the decision you've made and I'm treating as fixed. It is independent of point 1: an apology can be delivered at dessert, or before Sunday by phone or in person, and doesn't require sitting through the meal.

On your mother's forecast: "look bad forever" is a prediction, not an observation, and two days out nobody can know how this reads in six months. What is checkable is that an unretracted personal insult, left standing while you skip most of the meal, is the version most likely to be repeated. A specific apology for the words removes that.

Message to your mother (spoken, not text):

> "I'm going to apologise to Salma for what I called her — that was wrong and I'll say so, to her, either before Sunday or when I arrive. I'm not going to apologise for the leave or for defending it, and I'm still coming for dessert only. You don't have to agree with me or defend me to anyone; I've already told Tarek and I'll take whatever comes from that myself."

That does three things: gives her the part of what she asked for that is defensible on the facts, states the boundary in one sentence, and explicitly releases her from carrying it. She doesn't have to pick a side because you're not asking her to say anything to anyone.

Next action: decide whether the apology to Salma happens before Sunday (a call today or tomorrow) or at dessert. Before Sunday is lower-stakes — no audience — and means dessert isn't the first contact since the argument.

I hear you on keeping the descriptions at what I can defend. And you're right, I can apologise for the words without apologising for the leave. I'll call her tonight (hate the idea, but no audience is better).

The call has one job: retract the words. Keep the scope that narrow.

**What to say:**

> "I'm calling about Saturday. I called you a bitter, miserable old woman. That was wrong and I'm sorry I said it."

Then stop. Don't add "but you've been…" — the apology is for your conduct, and any "but" converts it into a counter-charge and restarts the argument.

**What to have ready if she responds by restating her view of the leave:**

> "I'm not going to discuss the leave. I called to apologise for what I said, and I've done that."

Repeat once if needed, then end the call. You are not obliged to stay on the line for a second round of the exchange you're apologising for.

**What to avoid:**

- Asking her to apologise in return. It may or may not come; making it a condition turns a retraction into a negotiation.
- Explaining why you lost your temper. Any explanation is heard as justification.
- Mentioning the building decisions. There's still nothing on record connecting her to them.

**Length:** under two minutes if she accepts it; under five if she doesn't.

After the call, tell your mother it's done. That closes the part of her request you agreed to and leaves Sunday's timing as the only open point, on which you've already messaged Tarek.
